newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter's Lombard unit sees expansion.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter's Lombard unit sees expansion.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover Co said on Wednesday its recently-acquired on-line brokerage, Lombard Brokerage Inc, would change its name to Discover Brokerage Direct and offer expanded services.

Dean Witter, which just completed a merger with Morgan Stanley, agreed to buy San Francisco-based Lombard in December. The company said it would leverage existing strengths in each entity and expand product offerings.

Stephen Miller, senior executive vice president and regional director at Dean Witter Discover, will become chairman and chief operating officer of the new enterprise, while Lombard founder V. Eric Roach wild be president, it said.
Miller and Roach told a conference call they were considering offering a variety of services to customers, including a co-branded credit card and a savings account.
But both executives stressed that the strategies for the operation were still plans in progress.
"We are still undecided about some of the specifics but we are working with the different companies," Miller said.
New services and products, including tax preparation, bill payments, securities trading and financial planning would be wrapped around a customer's central asset account, they said.
Credit, mortgage, checking and insurances services might also become available, they said.
The on-line brokerage would also participate in Microsoft Corp's Microsoft Investor, an on-line investing resource, they said.
"We would like to create a living, breathing assett statement for each customer," Roach said. "The customer would be able to define what services they wanted from us as opposed to other customers."
As Discover Brokerage Direct rolled out these services in scale, it would access other core components of Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter, they said.
"We will be able to leverage and link the capabilities of Morgan Stanley down the road, including the global capabilities," Roach said.

Demographic studies and market research showed Lombard customers shared a similar profile with Discover card customers, they said. Customers would relate to the Discover brand name, the executives said.
"Lombard customers are younger than Dean Witter customers and more trading oriented," Roach said.
